findings.where: Screen 6 demo and screen 13 after Check, clock card name and Hour / Clockwise readouts
findings.what: While the a–b hand sweeps an hour per quarter-second, the name under the clock and the readouts tick through Dyn0, Dyn2, Dyn3 and Dyn4 (Dyn2 to Dyn6 on screen 13), groups a delta-star cannot have, so the motion suggests that swapping the ends turns the output gradually through real groups; hold the old name and readouts, or show a dash, until the hand lands.
"Line voltage A–C sits at two o'clock, 60° behind A–B" is stated without the step; one short sentence (A–C is C–A turned round, and C–A sits at eight) would complete the why.
"30° ahead" turns into "one hour anticlockwise" with no sentence saying phasors turn anticlockwise, so ahead means anticlockwise; that link first appears in screen 7's hint.

The words work the one-hour Yyn0 case (5.2 times rated) first, but the demo leaves Yyn0 after 0.6 s without closing the switch and closes only at Dyn5; close at Yyn0 first so the bar shows 5.2 before the 20.
After the switch trips open, the bar stays filled at 20 times rated under the label "Circulating"; label it "if closed" like the readout, or let it fall when the switch reopens.
"Through 5% + 5%, that drives 52 ÷ 10 = 5.2 times rated" skips the step that 10% of the voltage drives rated current round the pair.
At Dyn11 the two dashed limb-1 hands lie under the thick A–B hand, so the step the words rest on (a–n at twelve with A–B) is hard to see; offset or outline them.

The paralleling rule gives only ratio and group, though the brief promised matching impedance and ratings within two to one as well (impedance appears only as a rule of thumb in practice, rating not at all); the finish's "only with the same ratio and group" also drops the explain's "as connected".
"Running generators together brings checks of its own, beyond these." does not say that they come next, in Generators and paralleling.
"A three-phase transformer is three single-phase ones on one core" is stated as fact; the explain's "works like" is the honest form, since a three-limb core's fluxes share their return paths.
"You may meet Dyn11 described as a lag, so read it from the clock" leaves him unsure what the lag figure is; say it is a 330° lag, the same as 30° ahead.
The footnote sits on "Each hour is 30°", which is 360 ÷ 12 and not a figure he would look up; keep footnotes for the naming rule and the paralleling rule.
"5.2 × 502 = 2610 A" carries the rounded 5.2; the unrounded 5.18 gives about 2600 A, so "about 2600 A" is the honest figure.
"Still there." reads oddly on its own; a line such as "Right, you still have it." says what it means.
